entry.evidence: it has so far been difficult to differentiate between asthenospheric and lithospheric origins of observed seismic anisotropy

sequences.source_document: Published paper PDF, with XML captions

steps.action: States the open question of whether SKS splitting beneath the Alps reflects recent asthenospheric flow or fossil lithospheric deformation, given the weak depth resolution of SKS splitting.
steps.quote: has been under debate

steps.action: Lists published explanations of the Alpine splitting pattern: flow around the Western Alps, flow from European slab detachment, slab rollback, the Salimbeni counterflow, and fossil slab fabric.
steps.quote: Other explanations are either associated with flow generated by a European slab detachment

steps.action: Takes over the authors' 2020 procedure, which relates backazimuthal variations of non-vertically-incident SKS splitting to foliation orientation, and applies it to a new region.
steps.quote: developed a procedure to relate azimuthal variations of ϕ and Δt to foliation orientation and subsurface deformation

steps.action: Poses two end-member rivals: b-up olivine with horizontal foliation (Simple Asthenospheric Flow) and c-up olivine with vertical foliation (Vertical Coherent Deformation in the lithosphere).
steps.quote: Inferring from Silver (1996), we relate them to a Simple Asthenospheric Flow (SAF) and a Vertical Coherent Deformation (VCD) scenario.

steps.action: Uses the Taylor-expansion expressions (Davis 2003) and MSAT forward models of a 100 km layer of 70% aligned olivine, from the 2020 study, to predict opposite d1 polarity and thus opposite δϕ phase for b-up and c-up.
steps.quote: While a b-up orientation leads to a negative d1 value, a c-up alignment causes a positive d1.

steps.action: Compiles published individual SKS/SKKS splitting measurements (Barruol 2011, Qorbani 2015, Salimbeni 2018), keeps those with σϕ ≤ 20° (787 to 738 measurements; 285 in the study area) and maps a mountain-chain-parallel pattern that rotates clockwise.
steps.quote: Fast orientations (bottom, left) indicate a unimodal distribution around NE-SW related to the clockwise rotation of ϕ.

steps.action: Designs the test: takes station means (stations with at least five measurements), forms δϕ and δΔt, trims outliers at the 5% and 90% quantiles, and keeps ±33.25° windows around backazimuths where b-up and c-up predictions differ most.
steps.quote: where the expected difference between b-up and c-up olivine variation in δϕ is the largest

steps.action: Compares the means and medians of δϕ and δΔt, with 2σ errors, against the forward-modelled b-up and c-up curves for the whole study area; the data favour b-up, i.e. horizontal-flow (SAF) anisotropy.
steps.quote: suggests a b-up olivine situation in the study area and thus a horizontal flow plane of deformation as described by the SAF model

steps.action: Overlays the splitting on the Koulakov et al. (2009) P-wave tomography (150 km slice and profiles A-C) and finds that fast orientations follow the low-velocity (flow) and high-velocity (slab) anomalies.
steps.quote: For each of the two anomalies the fast orientation seems to follow the shape of the anomaly.

steps.action: Proposes that the anisotropy has different origins: flow-related in the northern low-velocity block and lithospheric (slab) in the southern high-velocity anomaly.
steps.quote: then the high-velocity anomaly in the south could comprise the origin of lithospheric anisotropy

steps.action: Computes vertically-integrated travel times through the Koulakov model (77.5-410 km) and uses their lateral variation to split the area into northern and southern subareas.
steps.quote: use the lateral variation as criterion to define subareas

steps.action: Repeats the travel-time calculation with the Hua et al. (2017) tomography; it gives a more complex pattern, and the authors keep Koulakov for the partition.
steps.quote: To ensure our distinction is not biased by the specific model, we also determine travel times for the model of Hua et al. (2017) in [...]

steps.action: Describes the subarea distributions: ϕ rotates more and Δt is higher (about 1.28-1.92 s) in the north; ϕ is NE-SW to ENE-WSW with lower Δt and sparser data in the south.
steps.quote: reveal a noticeable larger rotation (more pronounced spreading) of ϕ and a tendency to higher Δt in the northern subarea

steps.action: Applies the same backazimuthal test to each subarea: the north still suggests b-up but with lost uniqueness at 2σ; the south cannot be discriminated.
steps.quote: A stable differentiation between the b-up and c-up cases for olivine orientation (bottom), based on the non-vertically-incident SWS approach, is thus not possible

steps.action: Retains the claim that, in the joint analysis, the variations agree with b-up olivine and horizontal foliation produced by asthenospheric flow around the Alps.
steps.quote: variations agree with a simple model of olivine with a horizontal foliation and vertical b-axis

steps.action: Checks the single-layer premise of the method: the 360° signature of a dipping a-axis is not seen in δϕ or δΔt, the δΔt scatter stays within expectations, and crustal-layer and frequency-dependence effects are argued unlikely.
steps.quote: A key assumption of our analysis has been that the observed SWS is well-characterized by a single, horizontal layer of orthorhombic anisotropy.

steps.action: Rules out a girdle configuration of olivine (d1 ~ 0) and infers a high-temperature deformation mechanism instead.
steps.quote: Another intriguing consequence of our observations is that a girdle configuration of olivine grains

steps.action: For the northern flow, poses two rival flow types: planar Poiseuille (pressure-driven channel) flow and Couette (drag-induced) flow.
steps.quote: there are two simple flow types that are relevant at this spatial scale, planar Poiseuille flow

steps.action: Derives the strain profiles of both flows (Appendix B): Poiseuille gives twice the integrated strain for a given maximum velocity, and Couette implies fast orientations aligned with lithospheric motion.
steps.quote: It follows that Poiseuille flow is twice as efficient in generating strain (and SKS splitting) compared with Couette flow

steps.action: Estimates the thickness of the deforming layer from the low-velocity zone in tomographic profile B, noting the limits set by depth resolution and smearing.
steps.quote: which corresponds to a thickness of 180 to 200 km

steps.action: Compares fast orientations with GNSS surface motions (Sánchez et al. 2018) and finds an opposite sense of rotation.
steps.quote: A comparison reveals an opposite sense of rotation

steps.action: Rejects pure Couette flow (mantle flow coupled to lithosphere motion) and favours Poiseuille flow, driven by the pressure change from Apenninic slab rollback.
steps.quote: Poiseuille flow is therefore the more likely deformation model for the area.

steps.action: For the southern subarea, lists possible contributions: sub-slab flow, serpentinization, other olivine fabric types and increased lithospheric slab anisotropy, the last supported by lower splitting along profile C.
steps.quote: is likely increased in the southern part, following the steep incidence of the slab

steps.action: Concludes with b-up asthenospheric anisotropy for the area, a planar Poiseuille flow contribution channelled by the European slab in the north, and an unresolved south.
steps.quote: Instead a planar Poiseuille flow contribution, channeled by the European slab geometry beneath the Alps

end.claim: Backazimuthal variations of SKS splitting in the Central Alps indicate b-up olivine and thus horizontal-flow asthenospheric anisotropy, with a planar Poiseuille (channel) flow contribution around the European slab in the northern subarea.

decisive_move.sentence: Without the comparison of observed δϕ means and medians against the forward-modelled b-up and c-up curves, there would be no constraint distinguishing an asthenospheric from a lithospheric source.

gates.evidence: Action: no new data were acquired; the measurements were compiled from published studies, but the hypothesis predictions directed the choice of backazimuth windows where b-up and c-up differ most (p. 4). Claim: the opposite d1 polarity meant the data could have matched c-up instead; the GNSS comparison could have supported Couette flow (pp. 5, 11). Registration: the olivine model (70% aligned, b-up/c-up) was fixed from the 2020 study and fitted 'without adapting it' (p. 8); the σϕ threshold was set by testing on an earlier version of the data set, and the thresholds and intervals were adapted to the data volume (p. 4).

imports.item: Couette and planar Poiseuille flow between parallel plates (Brennen 2006; Richardson 2011)
CircStat circular statistics toolbox (Berens 2009) for mean fast orientations
Christoffel equation, via the Taylor expansion of Davis (2003)

novelty_claims.quote: This suggests that shear-wave splitting observations can in principle provide constraints that have so far not been recognized.
they have not been studied before

limits:
The supplied XML contains only figure captions, so all body text is located by printed pages. No review file or earlier version was supplied, so no review sequence is coded. No new seismic data were measured: the splitting parameters are other groups' published measurements (one coauthor is on Barruol 2011 and Qorbani 2015), and the analysis re-uses them. The b-up vs c-up decision rests on 2σ error bars of window means; no formal test statistic is given, and the 135° and 315° windows are sparse. The σϕ threshold was tuned on an earlier version of the data set (inference: partly data-informed processing).

Sub-claims at other statuses: Poiseuille over Couette flow in the north is best_explanation, based on one qualitative GNSS comparison; the girdle configuration being unlikely is best_explanation; the 180-200 km deforming-layer thickness is estimate_with_resolution, but no formal uncertainty is given; the southern subarea is no_conclusion. A lithospheric slab contribution in the south is suggested only.

Composition is coded strong_inference because of the crucial d1-polarity test between two rivals followed by refinement (SAF into Couette vs Poiseuille). Conditions are found rather than set, so trace_series is a defensible alternative. The northern Poiseuille interpretation depends on a single tomographic model (Koulakov 2009).
